column1: # The JM streams (names starting with c, l and q) were encoded with the JM reference encoder 19.1 (lencod,
# jvet/JM master 8b34eee, built from source) from its cfg/encoder.cfg with YUVFormat set to the chroma format,
# ProfileIDC=244, LevelIDC=30, HierarchicalCoding=0, InputFile holding ffmpeg 7.1's
# "testsrc2=size=WxH:rate=25,noise=alls=10:allf=t+u" in the 16-bit planar format of the chroma format with
# each plane shifted right to its bit depth (8-bit samples when both depths are 8), SourceBitDepth* and
# OutputBitDepth* set to the depths, and the parameters below; QmatrixFile=q_matrix444.cfg is cfg/q_matrix.cfg
# with distinct 8x8 Cb and Cr lists (INTRA8X8_CHROMAU 10+3x+2y, INTER8X8_CHROMAU 40-2x+3y, INTRA8X8_CHROMAV
# 12+4((x+y)%5)+x, INTER8X8_CHROMAV 20+5(y%3)+2(x%4) at column x, row y). The streams marked "pcm source" use
# so the noisy right half codes as I_PCM ("left pcm source": the left 32 columns, crop=32:64:0:0 and
# overlay of the right half). The JM decoder (ldecod) reproduces each encoder reconstruction, the expected
# hashes in frames.tsv are its output, FFmpeg's output matches for every stream with equal depths, and the
# lossless streams decode to their encoder input exactly.
# The separate-color-plane streams (names starting with m) were made by encoding each plane of such a 4:4:4
# source as a 4:0:0 stream with the JM encoder (the same parameters for the three planes) and merging the
# three into one stream with separate_colour_plane_flag: profile_idc 244, chroma_format_idc 3, the absent
# Cb and Cr 8x8 scaling lists, colour_plane_id inserted in every slice header, and the slices of each picture
# written Y, Cb, Cr. Each plane decodes as its monochrome stream does (ITU-T H.264 8, separate_colour_plane_flag)
# except for the choice of scaling lists, so the expected hashes are those of the three JM encoder
# reconstructions stacked, or, for the stream with scaling matrices, which each plane takes from its own lists,
# the output of the JM decoder. The JM 19.1 decoder agrees on the progressive streams without temporal direct
# prediction, fails on field pictures and differs on MBAFF with I_PCM and on temporal direct prediction of the
# The x264 streams (names starting with x) were encoded by FFmpeg 7.1 with libx264 (core 164 r3192) or
# "testsrc2=size=96x64:rate=25" filtered by "fade=in:0:8,noise=alls=8:allf=t"); FFmpeg and the JM decoder agree on
# every frame, and the lossless ones decode to their source exactly.
# frames.tsv also holds the hashes of the ITU-T Professional_profiles 4:4:4 conformance streams, which come
# without a reference YUV: the output of the JM decoder in Y, Cb, Cr order (JM writes the planes of streams with
# matrix_coefficients 0 as R, G, B), which FFmpeg's output matches for the streams it decodes.
